summary: One native run of loader-diag-xnu-run-usb under decision 0026 (decision 0019 protocol). The host computer received by itself, with no camera and no owner action, all 27 stop notes of the XNU kernel's boot code to C checkpoint 21, then the kernel was resumed with no further stop and ran on: the stub received the kernel's own return (reason-0 note n=28, x3=0x0) 1.7 s after the last stop, and the kernel's log (19510 bytes: its message buffer and panic buffer, 204 records) followed, then the loader's HOLD record: 386 frames, 384 records, contiguous, 0 drops, nothing unread, manifest complete-received-stream; the analyser verdict is PASS. The log shows the kernel past arm_init: GICv3 found and mapped (virtual timer PPI 27), VM and zone bootstrap, IOKit/PMRD start, the scheduler, BSD init up to the network stack, cpu_start and the framebuffer notice, then a panic by the kernel itself: IOFindBSDRoot: specified root memory device, md0, has not been configured (boot-arg rd=md0, no ramdisk). The first dump at checkpoint 21 was empty (loader_log held no live kprintf text then). The phone re-entered Download Mode by itself at T0 + 79.7 s (NAT-044 deadline reset); stock RECOVERY was restored with a full-hash match and Android was verified (boot_completed, user data directories present).

not_established: Whether timer interrupts are delivered by the GIC on this phone (scheduling and the counter-based clock need none; the loader_return_after timer never came due).

Whether the live kprintf -> loader_log_putc path is silent with serial=3: dump 1 at checkpoint 21 was empty and dump 2 consists of the message buffer and panic buffer that loader_return() appends; the run does not separate the two explanations.

What the kernel did to peripherals other than the GIC, timer and framebuffer notes (its MMIO reach is unbounded by review; nothing unexpected was observed); repeatability (one run); display output, GPU, storage, USB or any userland (the kernel never reached launchd).
The effect of 'pe_arm_map_interrupt_controller: failed to find the interrupt-controller' and 'pe_arm_init_debug: failed to find cpu-debug-interface' (printed although the GIC was found).
findings: The next obstacle is the root device: the payload's boot-args carry rd=md0 and no ramdisk exists, so BSD panics in IOFindBSDRoot at the end of bsd_init's device setup. A ramdisk (or boot-args without rd=md0 together with something that lets BSD proceed) is needed to reach the start of /sbin/launchd and a console.

The kernel's own log is the best available channel past checkpoint 21: the message buffer reaches the host at the kernel's return (panic, loader_return_after or halt). A kernel that does not return (hang) would give no text; the first dump (live loader_log) was empty.

Timeline (T0 = reboot request 2026-11-11T20:25:43.963Z): phone left the bus +3.7 s; 1209:0001 appeared +18.7 s; CK n=1 received +36.3 s; CK n=27 (checkpoint 21) +47.4 s; n=28 (kernel return) +49.1 s; log dump +49.15..+52.0 s; HOLD +53.0 s; 1209:0001 left +75.8 s (57.1 s after enumeration, as in NAT-058/060: the deadline reset); Download Mode +79.7 s; Android back +124.6 s.

The analyser's PASS says the chain was complete; it does not say the kernel is healthy. Kernel text timestamps contain unnormalised microsecond fields (e.g. 39.1000184), so host receive times are used for timing.
